# Funky Esset Maker

> Browser tools that turn text into a figure you can paste into a slide,
> handout, or paper — code listings, equations, tables, data structures,
> diagrams, plots, charts, number lines, truth tables, QR codes, and model
> architecture figures — plus one that converts between LaTeX and 한글(HWP)
> equation script. Everything runs client-side; nothing is uploaded.

This file is for an assistant helping someone use the app. The useful thing you
can do here is **write a project file**: a small JSON the user opens in the app,
which drops them straight into the right tool with their content already in it.

## Writing a project file

Every tool reads the same envelope. Save it as `something.json` and tell the
user to open it — sidebar **열기** (⌘O), or just drag the file onto the window.
The `tool` field is what selects the tool, so the user does not have to pick the
right one first.

```json
{
  "app": "funky-esset-maker",
  "format": 1,
  "tool": "<tool id from the table below>",
  "theme": "funky",
  "data": { }
}
```

- `data` is that tool's own state. Fields you leave out fall back to defaults,
  so send only what you are setting.
- `savedAt` (ISO string) and `name` are optional.
- Opening replaces whatever the user had in that tool. Say so if their work
  might still be in there.

### Render mode

`theme` is app-level, not per-tool, and it changes how *every* tool draws:

- `"funky"` (default) — neon fills, 2px black outlines, hard shadows. For
  slides and handouts.
- `"paper"` — hairline rules, serif labels, no fills behind text, and the
  Okabe–Ito colour-vision-safe palette. Tables become booktabs (three
  horizontal rules, no verticals). For papers and reports.

Set `"theme": "paper"` whenever the user says the figure is for a paper,
journal, thesis, or report. Leave it out to keep whatever mode they are in.

Colour and fill choices are kept in `data` either way — paper mode simply does
not paint them, so switching back restores the slide look. That means you can
set `headerColor`, `accent` and the rest even for a paper figure; they just
will not show until the user switches to funky.

Values shared by most tools:

- `bg`: `"transparent" | "cream" | "white" | "dark"` — transparent is best for
  slides, and is the default nearly everywhere.
- neon color names: `pink · purple · cyan · yellow · orange · sky · green`

### Print settings (`cartesian`, `chart`, `numline`, `qr`)

These draw as SVG and export true vector, so they also take:

- `widthId` — how wide the figure prints. `"screen"` (default, 1 px = 1/96 in),
  `"icml-col"` (3.25"), `"cvpr-col"`, `"acl-col"`, `"aaai-col"`,
  `"neurips-col"` (5.5"), `"icml-full"`, `"cvpr-full"`, `"acl-full"`,
  `"ieee-col"`, `"ieee-full"`, `"nature-1"` (89 mm), `"nature-2"` (183 mm),
  `"science-2"`, `"elsevier-2"`, `"pnas-2"`, `"slide"`.
- `dpi` — `150 | 300 | 600 | 1200`, for the PNG path only.

⚠️ Setting `widthId` alone is not enough. A 760 px figure printed at 3.25 in
has 4 pt labels. **Also set `figW` to the column width in pixels** — 96 px per
inch, so `"icml-col"` wants `figW: 312`, `"neurips-col"` wants `figW: 528`,
`"nature-2"` wants `figW: 691`. The app shows the resulting point size in the
toolbar and turns it red under 6 pt. (In `qr` the same readout is the printed
size of one module, red under 0.5 mm.)

## Tools

| `tool` | Makes | Content field |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `highlighter` | syntax-highlighted code | `codes` |
| `latex` | equations, or prose with inline math | `latex` |
| `tabler` | tables | `cells` |
| `dsviz` | lists and dicts as tables | `input` |
| `grapher` | boxes-and-arrows diagrams | `nodes` + `edges` |
| `aifig` | model architecture figures for papers | `nodes` + `edges` |
| `cartesian` | function / polar / implicit plots | `graphs` |
| `chart` | bar, line, pie, scatter | `input` |
| `numline` | number lines, intervals, inequalities | `input` |
| `truth` | truth tables | `input` |
| `hwpmath` | LaTeX ↔ 한글(HWP) equation script, either way | `latex` / `hwp` |
| `qr` | QR codes | `text` |

### highlighter — code

`codes` is keyed by language, and `lang` picks which one shows. `names` sets the
window's title bar per language (it also becomes the PNG's filename).

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"highlighter","data":{
  "lang":"python",
  "codes":{"python":"def solve(n):\n    return n * 2"},
  "names":{"python":"solve.py"},
  "theme":"dark","fontSize":18
}}
```

- `lang`: `"python" | "markdown" | "plain"` (unknown languages: use `plain`)
- `theme`: `"light" | "dark"` · `fontSize`: px
- `width`: px · `wrap`: bool · `crop`: bool with `cropHeight`, `ratioW`/`ratioH`

### latex — equations and documents

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"latex","data":{
  "mode":"math",
  "latex":"e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0",
  "fontSize":64,"color":"ink","bg":"transparent"
}}
```

- `mode`: `"math"` — one display equation per line (KaTeX).
- `mode`: `"document"` — prose with `$…$` inline and `$$…$$` display math.
  Supports `\textbf` `\textit` `\emph` `\texttt` `\underline`, `---` `--`,
  quotes, `\quad`, and blank-line paragraphs. Not full LaTeX: no environments,
  sectioning, or numbering. Set `docWidth` (px) or `docUnlimited: true`.
- `color`: `ink · white · pink · purple · cyan · orange · sky · green`
- Escape backslashes for JSON: `\\frac{a}{b}`.

### tabler — tables

`cells` is row-major; the first row is the header when `headerRow` is true.
Rows may be ragged, but keeping them equal avoids gaps.

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"tabler","data":{
  "cells":[["Model","Acc","Params"],["ResNet-50","76.1","25M"],["ViT-B/16","77.9","86M"]],
  "headerRow":true,"headerCol":false,
  "headerColor":"cyan","bodyBg":"white","align":"left","fontSize":30
}}
```

- `align`: `"left" | "center" | "right"` · `bodyBg`: `"white" | "cream"`

### dsviz — lists and dicts

One declaration per line. A list renders as a single-row table, a dict as a
two-column one. Nested brackets survive, so values may contain `(), [], {}`.

```
queue = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]
dist = {a: 0, b: 7, c: inf}
```

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"dsviz","data":{
  "input":"queue = [3, 1, 4, 1, 5]\ndist = {a: 0, b: 7, c: inf}",
  "showIndex":true,"accent":"cyan","fontSize":28
}}
```

`showIndex` puts positional indices above list cells.

### grapher — diagrams

Free-form boxes and arrows. `x`/`y` are top-left in canvas px; a box is about
150×50 by default and grows with its text. Every `id` must be unique, and each
edge's `source`/`target` must name a node.

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"grapher","data":{
  "nodes":[
    {"id":"a","x":220,"y":180,"text":"Input","color":"green"},
    {"id":"b","x":220,"y":340,"text":"Encoder","color":"cyan"},
    {"id":"c","x":220,"y":500,"text":"Output","color":"pink"}
  ],
  "edges":[{"id":"e1","source":"a","target":"b"},{"id":"e2","source":"b","target":"c"}],
  "snap":true,"transparentBg":true
}}
```

`color`: `surface` (white) plus the neon names. Space nodes ~160px apart
vertically so the arrows have room.

### aifig — paper figures

The heavyweight one: vector SVG output, LaTeX in any label, and column-width
presets. Its document is `{nodes, edges, canvas, paletteId}`, and missing
per-node fields are filled in on load — so a sparse figure like this works.

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"aifig","data":{
  "canvas":{"w":528,"h":327,"printWidthIn":5.5,"bg":"transparent"},
  "paletteId":"muted",
  "nodes":[
    {"id":"x","kind":"rect","x":40,"y":140,"w":90,"h":44,"label":"$x$"},
    {"id":"enc","kind":"trapezoid","x":180,"y":130,"w":110,"h":64,"label":"Encoder"},
    {"id":"z","kind":"cuboid","x":340,"y":138,"w":80,"h":48,"label":"$z$"}
  ],
  "edges":[
    {"id":"e1","from":{"node":"x","anchor":"auto"},"to":{"node":"enc","anchor":"auto"},"route":"ortho","endHead":"arrow"},
    {"id":"e2","from":{"node":"enc","anchor":"auto"},"to":{"node":"z","anchor":"auto"},"route":"ortho","endHead":"arrow"}
  ]
}}
```

- `kind`: `rect · cuboid · ellipse · op · diamond · trapezoid · cylinder ·
  stack · mlp · grid · brace · bracket · text · image · frame · curve ·
  triangle · parallelogram`
- `label` takes `$…$` inline LaTeX anywhere.
- `route`: `straight · ortho · curve · arc` · `endHead`/`startHead`:
  `none · arrow · open · dot · circle · diamond · bar`
- `paletteId`: `tab10 · muted · gray · okabe · tol`  (the last two are
  colour-vision-deficiency safe — prefer them for anything published)
- `canvas.printWidthIn` drives the printed point size; the app warns under 6 pt.
- The tool has 16 built-in templates (Transformer, ViT, U-Net, GAN, diffusion,
  …). For a standard architecture, tell the user to pick the template rather
  than generating one — it will be better laid out.

### cartesian — plots

Each entry's `expr` is **LaTeX** (the editor is MathLive). Escape backslashes.

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"cartesian","data":{
  "graphs":[
    {"id":"g1","expr":"y=x^{2}","enabled":true,"color":"#ff4eba"},
    {"id":"g2","expr":"y=\\sin\\left(x\\right)","enabled":true,"color":"#7828c8"}
  ],
  "xmin":-5,"xmax":5,"autoY":true,"grid":true,"figW":640,"figH":480,
  "widthId":"screen","dpi":600
}}
```

Accepted forms: `y=f(x)` · implicit `x^{2}+y^{2}=9` · polar `r=f(theta)` ·
a point `(1.5, 2.25) A` (trailing text labels it). Functions: `sin cos tan
asin acos atan sinh cosh tanh exp log ln sqrt cbrt abs floor ceil round min
max pow`, constants `pi e tau`. `^` is exponentiation. Set `autoY:false` with
`ymin`/`ymax` to pin the vertical range; `equalAspect:true` for circles.

### chart — bar / line / pie / scatter

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"chart","data":{
  "type":"bar",
  "input":"사과 = 30\n바나나 = 45\n체리 = 18",
  "title":"과일 판매량","showValues":true,"accent":0,"figW":640,"figH":440,
  "widthId":"screen","dpi":600
}}
```

- `type`: `"bar" | "line" | "pie" | "scatter"`
- bar/line/pie read `input`, one `label = value` per line.
- scatter reads `scatterInput`, one `(x, y)` per line.
- `accent` is a palette index (0–6) that rotates the series colors.

### numline — number lines

One item per line; each stacks into its own row above the axis.

```
x >= 2
(-1, 3]
[0, 4) 구간 A
3
open 5
```

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"numline","data":{
  "input":"x >= 2\n(-1, 3]\n5","auto":true,"figW":760,"bg":"transparent",
  "widthId":"screen","dpi":600
}}
```

Inequalities `x >= a`, `x < a`; intervals `[a,b] (a,b) [a,b)` — bracket vs paren
picks closed vs open; a bare number is a closed point, `open 5` an open one.
Trailing text after an item labels it. `auto:false` with `vmin`/`vmax` pins the
range. A trailing `#rrggbb` sets that item's colour explicitly — leave it off
and the item takes the mode's palette (neon in funky, Okabe–Ito in paper),
which is usually what you want.

### truth — truth tables

One expression per line; each becomes a result column. Variables are detected
automatically (up to 12).

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"truth","data":{
  "input":"p and q\np or not q\np -> q","useTF":true,"colorize":true,"header":"cyan"
}}
```

Operators: `not ¬ !` · `and ∧ &` · `or ∨ |` · `xor ⊕ ^` · `implies → ->` ·
`iff ↔ <->`, plus parentheses. `useTF:false` prints 1/0 instead of T/F.

### hwpmath — LaTeX ↔ 한글 equation script

The odd one out: it produces text, not a figure. 한글(HWP) has its own equation
language — `{a} over {b}` instead of `\frac{a}{b}`, no backslashes, spaces as
term boundaries — and this converts between the two, either way.

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"hwpmath","data":{
  "dir":"toHwp",
  "latex":"x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}"
}}
```

- `dir`: `"toHwp"` (default) rewrites LaTeX as 한글 script, which the user
  pastes into 한글's script input box (Ctrl+N, M). `"toTex"` goes the other way,
  for equations copied out of an existing 한글 document.
- `latex` and `hwp` are separate buffers, one per direction — set the one that
  matches `dir`. Send plain LaTeX in `latex`; surrounding `$…$`, `$$…$$`,
  `\[…\]` and `\(…\)` are stripped for you, and `\\` becomes 한글's `#`.

Reach for this whenever the user is writing in 한글 rather than LaTeX — a
Korean school or university document, a 보고서, a 문제지 — or whenever they
have 한글 equations they want in a LaTeX paper. Constructs with no equivalent
on the other side (blackboard bold, `\mathcal`, angle brackets going out;
LADDER, LONGDIV, REL coming back) still convert on a best effort, and the tool
lists what it had to approximate.

### qr — QR codes

`text` is encoded exactly as written — a URL, a sentence, a WiFi or vCard
payload string, anything. Everything else is how it looks.

```json
{"app":"funky-esset-maker","format":1,"tool":"qr","data":{
  "text":"https://ksa.hs.kr/festival",
  "ecl":"H","style":"rounded","eyes":"circle","fg":"#7828c8",
  "caption":"축제 안내","logoKind":"text","logoText":"✦","logoPct":0.2,
  "figW":420,"bg":"white","widthId":"screen","dpi":600
}}
```

- `ecl` — error correction, `"L" | "M" | "Q" | "H"`. `"M"` by default; go to
  `"H"` when there is a logo, or when the code will be printed small or on
  something that creases.
- `style` — module shape, `"square" | "rounded" | "dot"` · `eyes` — the three
  corner patterns, `"square" | "rounded" | "circle"`.
- `fg` — `#rrggbb` for the dark modules. It must be *dark against the
  background*: the app shows the contrast ratio and warns under 4:1, and neon
  on cream is around 2:1. Leave it out for near-black.
- `bg` — as elsewhere, but this tool defaults to `"white"`, not transparent. A
  transparent code on a dark slide has inverted contrast and no quiet zone.
- `caption` — a line of text under the code, `captionSize` its px size.
- `logoKind` — `"none" | "text" | "image"`. `"text"` draws `logoText` (an emoji
  or a couple of letters) in the middle; `"image"` needs `logoSrc` as a data
  URL, which the user is better off adding themselves by dropping a file on the
  code. `logoPct` (0.05–0.4) is the logo's width as a fraction of the code, and
  `logoWell: true` clears the modules underneath it.
- `quiet` — quiet zone in modules, 4 by the spec. Lower it only for a code
  already sitting inside plenty of white space.
- `minVersion` — 1 (default) picks the smallest symbol the content fits in.
  Raise it to keep a code the same size while its content is edited.

A logo can only hide as much as the error correction can rebuild: roughly
`logoPct²` of the symbol, against 7/15/25/30% for L/M/Q/H. `logoPct: 0.2` at
`"H"` is comfortable; the same logo at `"L"` is not. The tool says so on screen,
and refuses nothing — but a project that ships an unreadable code helps nobody,
so pair a logo with `"ecl": "H"`.

## Once it is open

- **PNG** — ⌘E saves, ⌘⇧C copies to the clipboard. Transparent background by
  default, so it drops onto any slide.
- **Vector SVG** — ⌘⇧E in `cartesian`, `chart`, `numline`, `qr` and `aifig`. The
  physical width is written in millimetres, so `\includegraphics{fig.svg}`
  lands on the column width with no scale factor. These four also rasterise
  their PNG from that same SVG, at up to 1200 dpi (2400 in `aifig`).
- **LaTeX source** — `tabler` and `truth` export a booktabs table, `highlighter`
  a `listings` block, `aifig` approximate TikZ. For a paper this beats an
  image: it matches the document's font and stays searchable. Suggest it
  whenever the target is a paper.
- **⌘S** saves the current tool back out as a project file, recording the
  render mode with it. **⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z** undo and redo in every tool (inside a text
  field the browser's own undo wins, which is the behaviour you want there).
- `hwpmath` has no image at all — ⌘⇧C copies its converted text instead.
- Work is kept in `localStorage` per tool, so a reload does not lose it.

## Editing after it opens

`cartesian`, `chart` and `numline` let the user click a curve, bar, slice or
interval in the figure and edit it in a side panel — value, label, endpoints,
colour, delete. Worth mentioning when you hand over a file that is nearly but
not quite right: adjusting one number is a click, not a re-generation.

## Getting it wrong gracefully

- A malformed field is usually replaced by its default rather than rejected, so
  a project can open looking subtly unlike what you intended — prefer sending
  fewer fields you are sure of.
- If `tool` is missing or unknown the app refuses the file and says so.
- A file saved by a newer version than the user's app is refused; tell them to
  reload the page.
